5904765730231937218:
At a wine shop beyond the northern frontier, Yi Dao and Chu Qingquan sat atop the roof.
Yi Dao had lost count of how much he'd drunk, his words slurring like thick mud. "Heh! What's the most... most important thing in life?"
He turned to Chu Qingquan. "Answer me!"
"Some value loyalty, some profit," Chu replied slowly, lifting his wine jar for a long swig. "Others... couldn't care less about anything but keeping their word."
"True enough. My Killerblade has ruled a lifetime—I fear no death! Just wouldn't dare face my parents as a man who broke his vows."
"Don't worry. I'll bear witness. You're a scoundrel, but when it comes to honor, no one matches you."
"Hahahaha! Drink—!"
"Enough. If you cause trouble drunk, it'll draw unwanted attention."
"Dammit, stop nagging! Since when does my drinking bother you?"
"Fine. Call it a night. I promise I'll personally offer you a jar of top-grade Parting Tears someday."
"Just one jar?"
"Ten jars."
"Deal! ...I'll hold you to that!"
Chu Qingquan fell silent, leaning against the roof tiles, murmuring something under his breath.
Yi Dao couldn't make out the words and grew annoyed. Chest itching from lack of wine, he staggered to his feet, drawing his blade to dance drunkenly.

It would be years before Yi Dao learned what Chu Qingquan had been reciting that night—a long poem:
"Three cups seal oaths that make Five Peaks bow low, 
Outweighing mountains high and steep."
"Drunk eyes blaze, heart hot, ears a-glow— 
As pride soars, piercing clouds deep and deep."

By the time Chu Qingquan finished reciting A Warrior's Journey, Yi Dao's Killerblade dance had also ended.
